Architectural overview

Problem & architectural thesis

Standard RAG pipelines let language models fabricate unsupported claims, silently merge conflicting sources, or write unverified assertions directly into persistent knowledge graphs. GIN separates probabilistic proposal from deterministic admission across decode-time token constraints, a sole-writer graph Bookkeeper, and trust-gated peer routing.

Control flow

  1. ProposeLocal LLM & Cartographer

    Retrieves candidate chunks and proposes continuations (Mistral-7B / Qwen2.5-7B) or inter-document relations.

  3. Deterministic GateSEAR Mask + Bookkeeper + Trust Gate

    Logits processor masks tokens outside verbatim corpus spans; Bookkeeper checks confidence floor, anchors, and DAG acyclicity; mTLS router checks peer domain trust.

  5. Commit / RefuseProvenance-Stamped State or Refusal

    Admits provenance-stamped graph nodes and grounded answers, or emits an explicit refusal when out-of-scope or untrusted.

Key tradeoff & failure mode

Verbatim decode constraints stopped token fabrication (0/21 on baseline, 0/50 adversarial decode trials), but cannot stop misleading juxtaposition or planted false sources (3/3 counterfactuals repeated). On the first all-layer stress run, production RRF peer selection dropped to 0.488 P@1, lexical-overlap verification accepted 15/16 adversarial probes, a forged peer chunk slipped through unverified, and issue-framing recall stayed 0/4 across 5 frozen encoders and 0/15 after patches.

What it is

  • GIN's SEAR layer constrains every generated token, at decode time, to continue a span that occurs verbatim in the retrieved corpus, using a custom llama-cpp-python logits processor. #gin-sear-decode-constraint
  • The Bookkeeper is the single admission gate for GIN's graph state: it checks a confidence floor, endpoint existence, self-loops, anchor integrity, duplicates and DAG acyclicity, then stamps provenance on what it admits. #gin-bookkeeper
  • GIN's federation layer passed its own bars for delegation, peer selection, per-domain trust gating and mutual TLS, on up to three nodes running on one machine. #gin-federation

BUILT LINKED #gin-stress-patched as of 2026-11-22

Patches to retrieval, the relation detector and federation, written against those failures, raised the same benchmark's scores: relation detector F1 0.686 to 0.982, production peer selection 0.488 to 0.872, retrieval top-1 0.914 to 1.000, stopword-trap refusal 4 of 5 to 5 of 5.

Does not showThat the fixes generalize. They were written after seeing failures on this exact set and re-scored on it, so these are fit scores, not held-out scores. One patch adds the exact units the set tests (euro, pound, km/h, GW, hectares). Issue-framing recall stayed at 0 of 15.

With a live Qwen2.5-7B on 12 stress queries, SEAR's no-continuation arm made 0 unsupported claims out of 13 and plain RAG made 3 out of 7. Both arms repeated planted false facts in 3 of 3 counterfactual queries, and SEAR answered one out-of-scope trap query it should have refused.

NEGATIVE-RESULT LINKED #gin-stress-first-run as of 2026-11-22

A new all-layer stress benchmark, built from this site's own open questions, found defects on its first run: the production peer selector picked the right peer for 0.488 of 86 remote queries (dense ranking alone: 0.884), the relation detector's precision on 105 contradiction pairs was 0.573, a pinned peer's forged chunk was relayed unverified, and the trust gate denied all 17 trusted-domain queries sent to a multi-domain peer.

Does not showPerformance on text GIN's author did not shape. The corpus and the 'blind-style' pairs were generated for this benchmark from this site's own open questions; nobody blind to the detector wrote them. All six nodes ran on one machine.

Where sources disagree

  • #gin-cartographer-stance The seed paired 0.632 -> 0.923 as one metric. In the spec, 0.632 is the within-event baseline and 0.923 is the cross-event-inclusive precision after the change; they are different metrics. The seed called the channel 'model-free'; the measured pipeline includes an NLI model. Verification stays AUTHOR-REPORTED because the numbers are in a spec's results section, not a committed eval output.
  • #gin-federation Seed said 'measured on a live 3-node deployment'. The artifacts show three nodes, all local to one machine.
  • #gin-nc-baseline The seed ledger said the Phase 1 fabrication result was 'model-independent across families'. The repo's model-independence claim is about the two-node divergence query sets (see gin-divergence-realtext), not this baseline, which ran on one model.
  • #gin-stress-patched stress_corpora.py says the pairs were 'written without tailoring' to the detector's internals. That held for the first run only: the patches that followed were tailored to the pairs, and a patch comment names the stress corpus.
  • #gin-judge-capability The seed merged this with the encoder sweep into one entry ('recall 0.000 across 5 encoders ... did not rise with model capability'). They are two experiments: the encoder sweep (0/4 for all five) and this judge sweep (non-monotonic, ending at 0/4).

Open questions

  • Does the relation detector hold on a corpus written by someone blind to its internals? (The 2026-11-22 stress set does not answer this: its author shaped both the set and the fixes.) from #gin-node6, #gin-cartographer-stance
    Would resolve it: Running Node6.
  • Do the stress-benchmark fixes hold on contradiction pairs and queries written after them? from #gin-stress-patched, #gin-stress-first-run
    Would resolve it: A fresh set written after the patches, ideally by someone who has not seen the detector; the patched code scored on it once, unchanged.
  • Is issue-framing contradiction a detectable signal, or a curatorial stance that labels cannot pin down? from #gin-encoder-sweep, #gin-judge-capability, #gin-framing-curator
    Would resolve it: More labeled pairs than four, ideally from more than one labeler.
  • Do the federation bars survive nodes on separate machines? from #gin-federation, #gin-tailscale-mesh
    Would resolve it: A multi-machine run of the same query sets.
